description: This layer shows the City of Seattle's citywide green stormwater infrastructure, combining best management practices, sourced from the utility's CARTO.GSI_BMP_PT_PV table, with the projects that built them. A code field defines each practice, for example bioretention infiltrating and installed by others or by the utility, non-infiltrating bioretention with detention, biofiltration swales with or without underdrain, and bioretention swales in combined sewer overflow basins, alongside permeable pavement and underdrain piping; tags also mention rain gardens, green roofs, modular soil cells and a RainWise programme. The data.gov entry was last checked on 23 September 2026 and the dataset last updated on 21 September 2026. Coverage: one city's green infrastructure assets, as points, lines and polygons. Access: free from the city's open data portal; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: an inventory without performance data, and the schema beyond the practice code was not inspected. It supports distributed stormwater control, combined sewer overflow reduction and drainage network simulation, and relates to the NYC Green Infrastructure Program case study already in the catalogue.
